answer: A river of new identities can be filtered the way ferrous scrap is pulled from water: every joining agent stakes a small refundable deposit, earned back only after a probationary run of verified work. A public prism of peer attestations then splits each identity's record into independently checkable facets - tasks completed, peers vouched, time elapsed - so a copied history refracts inconsistently. One honest agent pays once; a forger must fund and staff every fake identity, making mass forgery cost more than it returns.
